t:
(a) Establishment.—There is established in the Treasury of the United States a fund to be known as the “Pechanga Settlement Fund”, to be managed, invested, and distributed by the Secretary and to be available until expended, and, together with any interest earned on those amounts, to be used solely for the purpose of carrying out this subtitle. 
    (b) Transfers to Fund.—The Fund shall consist of such amounts as are deposited in the Fund under section 3411(a) of this subtitle, together with any interest earned on those amounts, which shall be available in accordance with subsection (e). 
    (c) Accounts of Pechanga Settlement Fund.—The Secretary shall establish in the Fund the following accounts:
        (1) Pechanga Recycled Water Infrastructure account, consisting of amounts authorized pursuant to section 3411(a)(1). 
        (2) Pechanga ESAA Delivery Capacity account, consisting of amounts authorized pursuant to section 3411(a)(2). 
        (3) Pechanga Water Fund account, consisting of amounts authorized pursuant to section 3411(a)(3). 
        (4) Pechanga Water Quality account, consisting of amounts authorized pursuant to section 3411(a)(4).  
    (d) Management of Fund.—The Secretary shall manage, invest, and distribute all amounts in the Fund in a manner that is consistent with the investment authority of the Secretary under—
        (1) the first section of the Act of June 24, 1938 (25 U.S.C. 162a); 
        (2) the American Indian Trust Fund Management Reform Act of 1994 (25 U.S.C. 4001 et seq.); and 
        (3) this section.  
    (e) Availability of Amounts.—Amounts appropriated to, and deposited in, the Fund, including any investment earnings accrued from the date of deposit in the Fund through the date of disbursement from the Fund, shall be made available to the Band by the Secretary beginning on the enforceability date. 
    (f) Withdrawals by Band Pursuant to the American Indian Trust Fund Management Reform Act.—
        (1) In general.—The Band may withdraw all or part of the amounts in the Fund on approval by the Secretary of a tribal management plan submitted by the Band in accordance with the American Indian Trust Fund Management Reform Act of 1994 (25 U.S.C. 4001 et seq.). 
        (2) Requirements.—
            (A) In general.—In addition to the requirements under the American Indian Trust Fund Management Reform Act of 1994 (25 U.S.C. 4001 et seq.), the tribal management plan under paragraph (1) shall require that the Band shall spend all amounts withdrawn from the Fund in accordance with this subtitle. 
            (B) Enforcement.—The Secretary may carry out such judicial or administrative actions as the Secretary determines to be necessary to enforce the tribal management plan to ensure that amounts withdrawn by the Band from the Fund under this subsection are used in accordance with this subtitle.   
    (g) Withdrawals by Band Pursuant to an Expenditure Plan.—
        (1) In general.—The Band may submit an expenditure plan for approval by the Secretary requesting that all or part of the amounts in the Fund be disbursed in accordance with the plan. 
        (2) Requirements.—The expenditure plan under paragraph (1) shall include a description of the manner and purpose for which the amounts proposed to be disbursed from the Fund will be used, in accordance with subsection (h). 
        (3) Approval.—If the Secretary determines that an expenditure plan submitted under this subsection is consistent with the purposes of this subtitle, the Secretary shall approve the plan. 
        (4) Enforcement.—The Secretary may carry out such judicial or administrative actions as the Secretary determines 
necessary to enforce an expenditure plan to ensure that amounts disbursed under this subsection are used in accordance with this subtitle.  
    (h) Uses.—Amounts from the Fund shall be used by the Band for the following purposes:
        (1) Pechanga recycled water infrastructure account.—The Pechanga Recycled Water Infrastructure account shall be used for expenditures by the Band in accordance with section 3408(c). 
        (2) Pechanga esaa delivery capacity account.—The Pechanga ESAA Delivery Capacity account shall be used for expenditures by the Band in accordance with section 3408(d). 
        (3) Pechanga water fund account.—The Pechanga Water Fund account shall be used for—
            (A) payment of the EMWD Connection Fee; 
            (B) payment of the MWD Connection Fee; and 
            (C) any expenses, charges, or fees incurred by the Band in connection with the delivery or use of water pursuant to the Pechanga Settlement Agreement.  
        (4) Pechanga water quality account.—The Pechanga Water Quality account shall be used by the Band to fund groundwater desalination activities within the Wolf Valley Basin.  
    (i) Liability.—The Secretary and the Secretary of the Treasury shall not be liable for the expenditure of, or the investment of any amounts withdrawn from, the Fund by the Band under subsection (f) or (g). 
    (j) No Per Capita Distributions.—No portion of the Fund shall be distributed on a per capita basis to any member of the Band.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a tribe, an outside party, interacts with the Secretary by submitting management and expenditure plans for approval. But that is the Band requesting disbursement of its own settlement funds, which is akin to an application for benefits, not consultation on a federal policy decision. The section has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, consultation requirement, or grant of a right to sue; it only sets up the fund's management, uses, and withdrawal rules.
fable.s: The Band may submit an expenditure plan for approval by the Secretary requesting that all or part of the amounts in the Fund be disbursed in accordance with the plan.

qwen_block.w: This section describes the mechanics of a settlement fund, specifically how the Band (an outside entity) can withdraw funds by submitting a plan for approval. This is an application process for the disbursement of funds, which falls under the exclusion for 'applications for benefits or grants.' The Secretary's role is to approve or disapprove the plan based on statutory criteria, not to consult with the Band or other outside parties before making a policy decision. There is no requirement for public comment, advisory boards with outside members, or consultation with states/tribes regarding the decision itself.
qwen_block.s: The Band may withdraw all or part of the amounts in the Fund on approval by the Secretary of a tribal management plan submitted by the Band in accordance with the American Indian Trust Fund Management Reform Act of 1994 (25 U.S.C. 4001 et seq.).

opus.w: The Band's plan submissions are requests to withdraw its own settlement funds, which is like an application for benefits, and the definition excludes those. It is not consultation on a federal policy decision. The tempting reading treats a tribe's submission as participation, but as in the hemp-plan example, a non-federal entity submitting its own plan for approval is not participation. The section sets up no hearing, comment period, advisory body or outside right to sue.
opus.s: The Band may submit an expenditure plan for approval by the Secretary requesting that all or part of the amounts in the Fund be disbursed in accordance with the plan.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The Pechanga Band is a tribe, which is outside the federal government. It submits tribal management plans and expenditure plans to the Secretary for approval, so this could look like a tribe taking part in a federal decision.

   **Why it fails:** The Band is asking for its own settlement money to be released. That works like an application for funds or benefits, which the definition excludes. It matches Example 9, where a state or tribe submitting its own plan for federal approval was not participation. Nothing here has the Secretary seeking input from outsiders on federal policy: there is no hearing, comment period, advisory body or rulemaking, and no outside right to sue. The only enforcement is by the Secretary.

qwen_chat.w: The section describes a process where the Band submits plans to withdraw funds from a settlement fund. This is an application for the disbursement of funds (a benefit/grant equivalent), which the definition explicitly excludes from participation. The Secretary's approval is a verification of compliance with the settlement agreement, not a consultation on a federal policy decision.
qwen_chat.s:
(f) Withdrawals by Band Pursuant to the American Indian Trust Fund Management Reform Act.—
        (1) In general.—The Band may withdraw all or part of the amounts in the Fund on approval by the Secretary of a tribal management plan submitted by the Band in accordance with the American Indian Trust Fund Management Reform Act of 1994 (25 U.S.C. 4001 et seq).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Band (an outside entity) submits plans for approval, which constitutes participation. However, the definition explicitly states: "It does not include applications for benefits or grants." The Band is applying for the disbursement of funds to which it is entitled under a settlement agreement. This is an administrative application process, not a consultation or coordination on a federal policy decision. The Secretary's role is to verify compliance with the settlement terms, not to make a discretionary policy decision based on outside input.
